title: Replace agentic.nvim with codecompanion.nvim (ACP, claude_code + opencode)
description: ai_assistant.lua configured carlos-algms/agentic.nvim with the opencode-acp provider. Replaced it with olimorris/codecompanion.nvim, using its ACP interaction by default, restricted to exactly two ACP providers: claude_code and opencode (adapters.acp.opts.show_presets=false plus explicit claude_code/opencode entries via adapters.extend). Kept equivalent keybindings under the <leader>a* namespace, renaming <leader>ad to <leader>aD to avoid an existing collision with a telescope Anki-deck picker mapping, and dropping the old agentic-widget-specific focus-toggle hack (<leader>af) since CodeCompanion's chat buffer is a normal window reachable via standard <C-w> navigation.
close_reason: Replaced carlos-algms/agentic.nvim with olimorris/codecompanion.nvim in lua/core/plugins/ai_assistant.lua. Configured adapters.acp with show_presets=false and explicit claude_code/opencode entries only; interactions.chat.adapter defaults to opencode (ACP). Verified via headless nvim that lazy.nvim installs/loads the plugin, the resolved config matches (default adapter=opencode, acp keys={claude_code,opencode}), :CodeCompanionChat/:CodeCompanionActions commands exist, and all new keymaps (<leader>ac/<leader>an/<leader>aC/<leader>aD/<C-a>) register in the correct modes without colliding with existing mappings. lazy-lock.json updated minimally (agentic.nvim removed, codecompanion.nvim added) after reverting an unrelated bulk plugin-update side effect from testing.
